All other posts stayed under 10. So I'm staying in the human body niche with an untouched topic: breath-holding. It fits the same pattern of an everyday action with hidden physiology, and every fact is well documented. Reel format, 5 short slides, as the strategy says. I'm using lofi music again since our best reel used it. For the hook test I'm running version B: a direct claim instead of a question. I'm rotating to palette 0. topic: Breath-holding physiology: CO2 urge, dive reflex, spleen, blackout, record
hook: What holding your breath really does

slides.title: It's not about oxygen
slides.body: That burning urge to breathe comes from carbon dioxide building up in your blood, not from running out of oxygen.
slides.image_prompt: Rising air bubbles in deep blue water lit by sunbeams from above, calm and mysterious

slides.title: Your heart slows down
slides.body: Put your face in cold water and the dive reflex kicks in, slowing your heartbeat to save oxygen.
slides.image_prompt: Glowing red heart shape sinking slowly into icy blue water, soft light, minimal

slides.title: Your spleen squeezes
slides.body: Your spleen contracts and pushes extra red blood cells into your blood. Free divers rely on this boost.
slides.image_prompt: Red blood cells flowing through a glowing blood vessel, microscopic view, dark background

slides.title: Your brain overrides you
slides.body: On land, you would black out first. Then your brainstem restarts your breathing automatically.
slides.image_prompt: Anatomical brain model with the brainstem softly glowing blue, dark background, cinematic light

slides.title: The world record
slides.body: In 2021, Budimir Šobat held his breath for 24 min 37 s after breathing pure oxygen first. Don't try it.
slides.image_prompt: Stopwatch floating in deep blue ocean water surrounded by small bubbles, sunlight from above

cta: Follow for facts your body hides
caption:
The panic you feel when you hold your breath isn't your body running out of oxygen. It's carbon dioxide piling up in your blood and setting off the alarm.

Meanwhile your heart slows and your spleen squeezes out extra red blood cells, the same tricks seals use on deep dives. Facts from Guinness World Records and diving physiology research.

Time yourself right now: how many seconds did you last? Drop it below 👇
